body.statement: Can the handle in \(\text{def:legal-relative-handle}\) establish, for \(r_n=a_n/2\), \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M}P_n\!\left[\sqrt n\|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)-\Phi(p_n)\|_\infty>Q_{1-\alpha}\{E_{p_n,r_n}(G^*)\mid\widehat p_n\},\ B_n\ne\varnothing,\ M(\widehat p_n)>0\right]\le\alpha,\] together with uniformly vanishing probability of the fallback event \(\{B_n=\varnothing\}\cup\{M(\widehat p_n)=0\}\), including arrays with zero cells, simultaneous active-cut ties, and \(Q_{1-\alpha}\{E_{p_n,r_n}(G^*)\mid\widehat p_n\}\to0\), where each displayed conditional quantile uses the lower-quantile convention?
body.justification: This is now the sole all-array inferential target. It asks whether the measurable nearby-legal-base construction yields the displayed uniform joint comparison without support, cut-gap, cell-mass, or variance floors when the conditional envelope quantile may vanish.
body.gap: The explicit legal \(K=4\) singleton-cell proof refutes every even symmetric max-linear probe. A bounded oriented construction repairs parity and finite curvature only on that face. Global simultaneous-face pointwise domination, complete legal latent transfer with covariance traction, relative lower-quantile transfer for a non-even Gaussian maximum, and the exact-zero-scale branch remain unproved and are not supplied by regular, standardized, or positive-variance inference results.
body.consumer: This open question is the only route in the current core to an all-array uniform joint-coverage theorem. A positive resolution must supply all four missing global certificates; until then, the proved measurability, width, separated-face calibration, \(K=4\) diagnostic, negative symmetric certificate, and singleton-face oriented ray do not yield theorem-level uniform coverage.

obligation.what_is_open: This is the sole all-array inferential target: prove the displayed uniform legal-inner-neighborhood comparison and conditional lower-quantile bound over arbitrary triangular arrays, including arrays for which the common envelope scale and its \(1-\alpha\) quantile converge to zero.
obligation.obstruction: The explicit legal \(K=4\) singleton-cell proof refutes every even symmetric max-linear probe of the form \(\max_\nu|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}z|\).  The bounded oriented construction repairs parity and finite curvature only on that singleton face.  Global pointwise domination across simultaneous capacity, selection-total, and active-cut faces; complete legal latent-mass transfer with row-by-row covariance traction; relative lower-quantile transfer for the resulting non-even Gaussian maximum; and the exact-zero-scale local-flatness branch all remain unproved.
obligation.attempted: The symmetric route sought an even finite maximum of linear rows dominated by the legal envelope and capable of controlling ambient endpoint increments; the explicit \(K=4\) singleton-cell certificate disproves that route.  The distinct oriented route retained signed one-sided rows and successfully constructed a legal survivor-to-never-selected transfer on the singleton face, yielding the required parity and finite-curvature inequalities there.  Extending those oriented rows through simultaneous faces did not establish pointwise domination by the full legal envelope, a complete latent-transfer and covariance-traction certificate, relative non-even lower-quantile validity, or the exact-zero-scale branch.
obligation.partial_result: The following results remain proved: the legal observed-law image, nearby-base envelope, conditional critical value, and total rectangle are measurable; uniformly over \(P_n\in\mathcal M\), the fallback probability vanishes and the finite coordinate widths are \(O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\); every fixed separated regular face has exact oracle Gaussian \(1-\alpha\) calibration; the explicit \(K=4\) emerging-support, rare-atom, tied-cut diagnostic has the stated Gaussian limit and exact limiting coverage; the singleton-cell construction refutes every even symmetric-probe reduction; and \(\text{prop:oriented-probe-frontier}\) records that the oriented ray repairs parity and finite curvature on that singleton face.  None of these partial results establishes the displayed all-array comparison.
